scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.
evidence.value_checked: gate:paginated-order-totality | 176 chains scanned, 0 non-total, forward-only PASS | selftest both directions | caught+fixed this session: report-sender.html:1357 order(triggered_at) | depends_on: community.html, tools/validate_paginated_order_totality.py, utils.js
evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate paginated-order-totality re-ran green against the current state (paginated_order_totality_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.
evidence.value_checked: gate:units_at_boundary | MIXED-SCALE 0 (the hard invariant) | UNDECLARED 2: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent), service_credit_ledger.amount (money) | undecl-latent 5 | PASS with debt | depends_on: community.html, tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py, utils.js
evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate units_at_boundary re-ran green against the current state (units_at_boundary_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: every response this page's reads receive carries the envelope shape its client expects
withdrawn_evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 9 read relation(s), 5 were probed live at the gateway (community_posts, community_reactions, community_replies, community_xp, hive_audit_log).  PLATFORM RESULT: across 40 relations, ZERO envelope defects and ZERO status/body disagreements. The error envelope is well-formed - {code, message, details, hint} on every error body, 400 (not 500) for an unknown column, 406 with PGRST116 for a single-object read of 0 rows, and a Content-Range header whenever Prefer: count=exact is asked. The status always agrees with the body: no 2xx carries an error object and no 4xx omits a machine-readable code. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - values_survive_write extracts every trigger that assigns to NEW, classifies the rewrite by its STRUCTURE, and fails on any that belongs to no named class. evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, which asks the oracle's question in the two halves it actually has.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, which asks the oracle's question in the two halves it actually has. STRUCTURE - WHO SEQUENCES THE WRITE, read out of pg_trigger and pg_proc rather than guessed. A page that writes two tables through two awaited client calls has NO transaction around them: a 500, a closed laptop or a dead network between the two leaves the first applied and the second missing, and nothing errors afterwards. A page that writes one table and lets a TRIGGER or an RPC write the second is atomic by construction, because one statement is one transaction. LEDGER - WHETHER A HALF-WRITE IS VISIBLE TODAY: 14 of 14 declared conservation invariants were checked against live data and ALL HOLD - the inventory running balance, transactions with no orphan item, every reply and every live safety post carrying its XP award row, no XP row outliving a deleted post unreversed, no staged reservation both consumed and released, one AMC briefing per hive per shift date, a scope item not completed twice, no project child outliving its project. ★AND THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A LINK, which is what stops 'client-sequenced' from being a verdict about the tool: the control pair community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards is joined by the trigger handle_community_post_xp, and the detector finds it. A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ROSTER-WIDE: 11 pages client-sequenced, 11 single-or-no-write. FOR THIS PAGE THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ORACLE, so this is NOT banked green even though nothing is broken today. The page writes community_posts + community_reactions; community_posts + community_replies; community_posts + hive_audit_log and the database does NOT link them - no trigger, no single RPC that writes both. So the first clause of the oracle ('either lands whole or not at all') is false as a structural matter: a failure between the two client calls leaves the first applied and the second missing, silently. WHAT THE LEDGER SAYS IS THE OTHER HALF, and it is genuinely reassuring rather than decorative: every declared conservation invariant holds against live data, so no half-write has HAPPENED. But 'has not happened yet' is a statement about this dataset, not about the code - the same shape as a latent null-collapse that no row has triggered. Banking it green would convert an absence of evidence into a guarantee. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either the second write moves behind a trigger or an RPC (making it atomic by construction, which is what 11 of the 22 pages already do and what the control pair demonstrates), or a probe interrupts the page BETWEEN the two calls and shows the ledger invariant catching the resulting half-state - which would prove the second clause with teeth instead of by absence. ★CORRECTION TO THE STRENGTH OF THIS CLAIM, made after reading what the pairs actually are. The prover enumerates every PAIR OF RELATIONS a page writes and asks whether the database links them - a cartesian over the page's write set, NOT a list of observed co-writes. Most of these pairs are therefore not one logical write split in two: community_posts + community_reactions are two separate user actions, asset_nodes + inventory_items are two different edits, and hive_audit_log pairs with everything because it is appended alongside many actions. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, asking the oracle's question in the two halves it has.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, asking the oracle's question in the two halves it has. STRUCTURE - WHO SEQUENCES THE WRITE, read out of pg_trigger and pg_proc rather than guessed: a page writing two tables through two awaited client calls has NO transaction around them, so a 500, a closed laptop or a dead network between them leaves the first applied and the second missing, and nothing errors afterwards. A page writing one table and letting a TRIGGER or an RPC write the second is atomic BY CONSTRUCTION, because one statement is one transaction. LEDGER - WHETHER A HALF-WRITE IS VISIBLE TODAY: 14 of 14 declared conservation invariants checked against live data and ALL HOLD. ★AND THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A LINK, which is what stops 'client-sequenced' from being a verdict about the tool: the control pair community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards is joined by the trigger handle_community_post_xp and the detector finds it. A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ★ROSTER: {"client-sequenced": 11, "single-or-no-write": 11}. FOR THIS PAGE THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ORACLE, so this is NOT green even though nothing is broken today. It writes community_posts + community_reactions; community_posts + community_replies; community_posts + hive_audit_log and the database does NOT link them - no trigger, no single RPC writing both - so a failure between the two client calls leaves the first applied and the second missing, silently. Every declared invariant holds against live data, which is genuinely reassuring, but 'has not happened yet' is a statement about this dataset, not about the code; banking it green would convert an absence of evidence into a guarantee. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the very functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

evidence.asserts: A multi-row or multi-table write either lands whole or not at all; a half-applied write is visible as an inconsistency in the ledger. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - write_atomicity exercises every declared ledger invariant live, inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK, and checks that the paired halves of a write cannot come apart.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every declared ledger invariant holds against the live database, exercised transactionally rather than reasoned about. The exposure the gate reports rather than hides is the honest part: 11 pages sequence TWO writes client-side, which is structural risk (a tab closed between them leaves the second undone) and is recorded as exposure, not counted as a failure, because no half-write has actually occurred in the data. That distinction is the same one this platform learned the hard way from a one-sided ledger write that passed every guard - the difference between "this could come apart" and "this has come apart" decides whether you are hardening a path or repairing rows. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration or function under this claim still expires it, and replay re-earns it in one command instead of a browser session.

evidence.asserts: What one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS: a value is not silently rewritten on the way in by something nobody named. evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). It earned that by first FAILING on a trigger I had added earlier in this same session: tg_community_posts_moderation_fields, which restores flagged/pinned for a caller who is not a supervisor of that hive (migrations ...000063/64, after a reported author was found clearing their own flag). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.

evidence.checked: PASSES, proven as a DECLARED invariant against live data: 'one person cannot react twice to the same post' returns ZERO offending rows. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT COMPARISON FOR THIS ORACLE: community's CD oracle: the reaction count must equal DISTINCT reactors, so a second row for the same (post, worker) would inflate a reputation signal that feeds the marketplace trust surface. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any offending row at all - the check reports the offenders by id, and two of the twelve invariants in this table did report offenders on their first run, so the instrument is known to fire rather than merely staying quiet. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: as a DECLARED invariant checked against live data, in the same table the ledger invariants live in - extended rather than given an eighth prover of its own. Each invariant names WHAT it compares and WHY that is the right comparison, because one wrong entry silently converts a real violation into a pass; this is the 'an exclusion must name its mechanism' discipline the order-totality gate already applies. Twelve invariants now run, ALL HOLD live, and the run carries a non-vacuity control (the trigger-linkage detector must see community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards, or a detector matching nothing would call every write pair on the platform unlinked). TWO OF THESE INVARIANTS WERE WRONG WHEN FIRST WRITTEN AND WERE CORRECTED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BANKED, both by reading the data rather than trusting the query. (1) 'a scope item is not completed twice', keyed on scope_item alone, reported 200 offenders - because a PM is RECURRING, so a monthly scope item legitimately carries a completion every month and the measured maximum is 12 distinct completion dates. A year of correct data read as a defect. Narrowing to the same DAY still reported 88, and those proved to have 2 or 3 DISTINCT workers at 2 or 3 DISTINCT timestamps - different people signing off the same item, not one write landing twice. The trigger-fires-once defect the oracle names looks like ONE worker at ONE instant with TWO rows, which is what the invariant now asks. (2) The orphan-hold check found one real offender and it is EXCLUDED BY ID WITH ITS REASON WRITTEN DOWN: reservation 39357091 holds part hd-bsk-1784479694 on 'Inventory Test Asset (H-scenario)', residue from a scenario walk whose part was removed, with neither consumed_at nor released_at set. It is a genuine dangling hold, it stays visible in the report, and excluding it keeps the gate able to catch a NEW orphan instead of being permanently red on known test debt. AND THE INVARIANTS THAT COULD NOT BE EXPRESSED WERE LEFT OWED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED - notably 'original budget + sum of approved change orders = current budget', because `projects` stores only budget_php (the current figure) and no original, so there is nothing to compare against.

Most numbers on this platform are COUNTS - 9 open jobs, 28 PMs overdue - and a count has no unit to show; flagging those would redden every surface, and a check that reddens everything is measuring itself. So 'MTBF: 45' fails, 'MTBF: 45 days' passes, and 'Open Jobs: 9' is never asked. ★THIS VIEW RENDERED ZERO DIMENSION-LABELLED QUANTITIES ON ITS DEFAULT STATE, so the check ABSTAINS rather than passing. An oracle's vocabulary IS the oracle. Both are fixed and recorded in the tool. evidence.checked: MEASURED LIVE, read-only, with tools/prove_number_labelled.mjs (no clicks, no writes): 11 number-bearing element(s) on this page's default view, 11 labelled, 0 UNLABELLED, and the instrument's own control check passed (ctl=ok) so a page that could not detect a missing label would have reported itself rather than passing silently. 20 element(s) were excluded and the count is reported rather than hidden - identifiers like GEN-003 or '405 XP' read as numbers to a matcher but are names, so elements inside a link, a button, a table header, or carrying a data-* id are skipped. A 'number-bearing element' is defined narrowly: a LEAF element whose entire trimmed text is numeric after stripping currency, separators, % and a unit suffix - '9' and '61%' qualify, '9 open items carried over' does not because it labels itself. A label counts when it is non-numeric text of >=3 chars in the element's own aria-label/title or in an ancestor's text with the number removed, climbing at most 4 ancestors and only while that ancestor's subtree is section-sized or smaller (<=400 chars) - both bounds are load-bearing, because too tight invents defects (it once called analytics' fully-documented OEE hero unlabelled for being 35 chars too verbose) and too loose makes the pass free by accepting a whole section's prose as a label. TWO ORACLES, ONE TRUTH CONDITION - stated because it would be dishonest to present this as an independent second measurement. This bank's CM oracle `what_is_this_number` ('a person can state what the number means from the surface alone') is already green from this SAME instrument and this SAME reading; CE's `number_explained` asks 'a person can say what the number MEANS without leaving the surface'. Those are the same question in two lenses, so the same measurement settles both and no second walk was fabricated to make this row look separately earned. That two of the 200 slots ask one question is a FRAME observation, and it belongs to the roadmap's synthesis rather than to this row. SCOPE, precisely: this is V1 only. The prover walks the view each page OPENS ON, so the V2 row's second view (a modal, a sheet, a tab) is NOT covered by this reading and stays owed.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. findings.title: NOT BANKED - THE PROBE COULD NOT TELL THE TWO POSTS APART, AND THE NEAR-MISS IS THE FINDING.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED - THE PROBE COULD NOT TELL THE TWO POSTS APART, AND THE NEAR-MISS IS THE FINDING. The anatomy names 'public <-> community (the same post on two surfaces)' as this page's cross-page seam, so the test is: a post marked public appears on BOTH surfaces, and a hive-only post appears ONLY on community. I drove it by matching a CONTENT SNIPPET on each surface. Both surfaces showed the text, and the 'hive-only' post appeared to render on the PUBLIC feed - which reads as a privacy leak, the single most serious defect this surface could have. ★IT IS NOT A LEAK. The seeded content is DUPLICATED across SIX posts with the same opening text: one public=true (085869d5) and five public=false (0f78265c, ed64b3ea, and three in other hives). public-feed was correctly rendering the PUBLIC copy; community was showing a hive-only copy; and my text match called them the same post. They never were. ★A CONTENT SNIPPET IS NOT AN IDENTITY. The post ids were available in the database and in the DOM the whole time - community renders each post in an element id'd 'post-<uuid>' - and I matched on text because it was the easier thing to see. On an oracle whose entire claim is 'the SAME object reads the same in two places', identity is the one thing that cannot be approximated. WHAT THIS WOULD HAVE COST: reporting that a hive-only post leaks to the public feed, on a platform where post visibility is stated BEFORE posting and is the thing a person cannot take back. A false privacy defect is not a harmless over-report - it would have sent someone to 'fix' a filter that is working correctly. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is small: match on the POST ID, not the text. Pick a known public id and assert it renders on both; pick a known hive-only id and assert it renders on community and NOT on public-feed. The counts already discriminate - 15 public platform-wide, 7 public in this hive, 24 hive posts total - so a mis-scoped read is visible in the numbers as well as the identity.

Both surfaces showed the text, and the hive-only post appeared to render on the PUBLIC feed. It was not a leak: the seeded content is duplicated across SIX posts sharing the same opening line - one public=true (085869d5) and five public=false (0f78265c, ed64b3ea, plus three in other hives). public-feed was rendering the PUBLIC copy; community was showing a hive-only copy; the text match called them one post. A content snippet is not an identity, and on an oracle whose claim is 'the SAME object reads the same in two places', identity is the one thing that cannot be approximated. ★ATTEMPT 2 MATCHED ON POST ID, AND ITS OWN POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED - which is what saved it. On community both ids resolved (#post-<uuid>, rendered). On public-feed NEITHER resolved, including the PUBLIC post that must be there. So 'the hive-only post is absent' rested on a selector that found nothing at all, and absence-by-blind-instrument is not absence. Reading renderCard() explains it: public-feed emits `<div class="post-card">` with NO id and NO data attribute, so a post's identity is not in that DOM at all. Identity matching there is impossible by construction, not by accident. ★ATTEMPT 3 COMPARES THE SET, which this surface can support: public-feed renders exactly 15 .post-card elements, all with real boxes, and the database holds exactly 15 posts with public=true and deleted_at null. The figure DISCRIMINATES rather than coinciding: this hive alone holds 24 non-deleted posts and only 7 public ones, so a feed that leaked hive posts would read 24-ish, and one scoped to a single hive would read 7. It reads 15 - the platform-wide public set, which is what a public feed is. WHAT IS PROVEN: the public feed shows the public set, exactly, and nothing more. WHAT IS NOT: that a SPECIFIC post appears on both surfaces with matching reply and reaction counts - that needs a stable identity in public-feed's DOM (a data-post-id on the card would settle it, and would also make a public post linkable, which it currently is not).

evidence.asserts: repeating an identical write does not create a second record, and the guarantee is enforced by a constraint rather than by the client
evidence.checked: PROVEN BY REPEATING THE WRITE, inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member. The same row - same primary key, same payload - was inserted twice in one transaction. The second attempt was refused: 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint logbook_pkey'. So a repeat cannot create a second record, and the guarantee comes from a CONSTRAINT rather than from client-side de-duplication that a double-tap, a retry, or an offline queue drain could outrun. WHY THE CONSTRAINT IS THE RIGHT PLACE FOR IT: this platform queues field-capture writes offline and drains them on reconnect, so the same logical write can genuinely arrive twice from two directions. A uniqueness guarantee that lives in the page dies with the page's assumptions; one that lives in the index holds for the queue drain, the retry and the second tab alike. VERIFIED CLEAN: 0 probe rows survived. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13. SCOPE: this settles the REPEAT of an identical write. It does not settle a second write with a DIFFERENT client-generated id representing the same intent - that is the offline-queue collapse question and lives on its own seam row.
evidence.value_checked: second identical insert refused by logbook_pkey; 0 rows after rollback

findings.detail: NOT PROVEN, AND THE REASON IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN 'NO PAIR FOUND'. Ten cross-surface pairs are proven across the roster with live discriminators, so the instrument works and a gap here is a fact about this page, not about the tool. XP IS THE SHARED FACT AND IT IS CURRENTLY ZERO. community renders #profile-xp and both community and hive read community_xp, so the pair is real - but community_xp for this worker is 0, and two surfaces both showing 0 agree for no reason. A comparison that cannot discriminate is not evidence, which is the rule this bank applies to its own discriminators, so it applies here too. SEPARATELY ESTABLISHED: hive renders no XP element at all, so the hive half of the roadmap's 'XP agrees across board and community' claim has no subject to read. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: seed XP for the probe identity (the triggers award it on posts and replies), then compare community's #profile-xp against the same figure wherever a second surface renders it. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FORCED: pairing two surfaces that answer DIFFERENT questions produces either a false red or, worse, a false green when the numbers coincide. This session made that exact mistake once - index's hive-wide open-jobs tile (9) against logbook's worker-scoped count (6) - and caught it only because they happened to differ. Had both read 6 it would have been banked as agreement. So an unforced pair is the safe direction here.

findings.title: MEASURED AND FAILING - 10 of 10 user-triggered write(s) on this page fire with NO connectivity check before them: toggleReaction, togglePin, toggleFlag, togglePublic, deletePost, submitPost, openPersonCard, markAnswer ….
findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - 10 of 10 user-triggered write(s) on this page fire with NO connectivity check before them: toggleReaction, togglePin, toggleFlag, togglePublic, deletePost, submitPost, openPersonCard, markAnswer …. THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED FIRST, because filing this against a page that is guarded elsewhere would be a manufactured finding: utils.js already defines whRequireOnline(action, notify) and exposes it as window.whRequireOnline, and it already carries the exact sentence this oracle asks for - 'You are offline. <action> needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.' The scanner's GUARD pattern matches RequireOnline( and navigator.onLine === false, so a page that called either would have counted as guarded. None of these writes call anything. This is NON-ADOPTION of a centralized, correctly-worded helper, not a missing message. WHY THE PLATFORM'S EXISTING GREEN DOES NOT COVER THIS: tools/validate_offline_write_guard.py PASSES at fail-severity, but its PAGES list is exactly ['marketplace.html', 'marketplace-seller.html'] - 19 writes on two pages. None of the 22 roster pages is in its scope, so its green says nothing about them. And widening that list alone would NOT be enough: the validator's user_invokable() recognises only window.X = and inline onclick/onchange/onsubmit, so of the 53 exposed writes measured across the roster it would see 37 and miss the 16 bound with addEventListener. WHAT A PASSIVE BANNER DOES NOT DO, since every page already adopts one: the banner states the condition, it does not refuse the action. The button still fires, the request still leaves, and the person still cannot tell whether their work landed - which is the whole distinction this oracle draws. THE FIX IS ONE LINE PER WRITE at the top of each function - if (!whRequireOnline('<gerund>', showToast)) return; - and the highest-stakes ones on this page should go first. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS after the guards land: prove it LIVE rather than statically, and note that setOffline does not flip navigator.onLine in the page, so the probe must override navigator.onLine AND block the network, then assert that zero requests fired and the sentence reached the person.

findings.title: MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean.
findings.detail:
MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean. ★THE INDUCTION IS PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED, which is the difference between a verdict and a guess: the lens reports inductionLanded, the number of reads that actually went out under the injected condition, and refuses to score a page that never re-queried. Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. A person whose data failed to load has nothing to press. ★ONE HALF OF THIS VERDICT IS INSTRUMENT-DEPENDENT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN BANKED AS FACT: the lens also reported saysFailure:False. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_retry_path.mjs (new) - EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then the network released and the retry pressed.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_retry_path.mjs (new) - EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then the network released and the retry pressed. ★THE INDUCTION IS TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL, AND THAT CHANGED THE ANSWER. The availability lens fails a SUBSET of reads and reported 'affordances: 0' for pages that demonstrably DO render a Retry on other paths. Failing every request is what actually reaches a page's error branch. ★AND BOTH CLAUSES ARE MEASURED, because the second is the one that ships broken: a retry must RE-ATTEMPT and the failure must CLEAR. hive proved why - its first fix sent 3 fresh reads and left the page byte-for-byte unchanged, because it re-rendered from a cache still holding the failed state. A retry that re-attempts and does not recover is worse than none: it invites pressing again. ★THE ROSTER, so no page's verdict rests on its own reading alone: PASS 6 (hive, logbook, inventory, skillmatrix, public-feed, resume) | NO-RETRY 9 | NO-RECOVER 3 | NO-ATTEMPT 1 | SILENT 3. ★THE COMPONENT ALREADY EXISTS - THIS IS ADOPTION, NOT DESIGN. whListError(el, message, onRetry) in utils.js renders the inline error WITH a working Retry, and 16 pages already import it. Six pages passing is what separates 'nobody built this' from 'not every read path routes through it'. FOR THIS PAGE THE RETRY IS THE DANGEROUS KIND: pressing it DOES re-attempt (7 fresh reads went out) and the failure is STILL ON SCREEN afterwards. That is worse than offering no retry at all - something visibly happens, so the person presses again, and again. hive had exactly this shape and the cause was re-rendering from a cache that still held the failed state; the fix was to point the retry at the loader that REFILLS that cache rather than the one that reads it.

The control that proved it: skillmatrix rendered Retry under the identical injection while hive and inventory did not - one page passing separates 'nobody built this' from 'not every read path routes through it'. ★THREE PLACEMENT/RECOVERY LESSONS, each caught by measuring rather than by looking: (1) hive's first fix re-attempted (3 reads) and left the page BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged - it re-rendered from a cache still holding the failed state; pointed at the loader that REFILLS the cache it recovered (13 reads). (2) pm-scheduler's targeted re-render restored the LIST while #pm-verdict-label kept saying 'Could not load PM compliance' - a PARTIAL recovery, worse than none, because the visible success invites trusting the rest. (3) shift-brain's retry rendered into #pms-list, which EXISTS and is HIDDEN: a control at height 0, real and correct and invisible, which the probe scored as no retry at all. ★AND THE PAGES THAT FAILED WERE MOSTLY HONEST ALREADY. asset-hub said 'unknown right now, not zero'; alert-hub said 'Reload before treating this plant as quiet'; project-manager said 'Reload before reporting status'. Saying the true thing and giving a way to act on it are two separate obligations, and only the first had been met. FOR THIS PAGE THE RETRY IS THE DANGEROUS KIND: pressing it DOES re-attempt (7 fresh reads) and the failure is STILL on screen. Worse than offering none - something visibly happens, so the person presses again. hive and pm-scheduler both had this shape; the cause each time was re-rendering from state that still held the failure, and the fix was to target the loader that rebuilds it.

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.
evidence.value_checked: 400-insert burst -> 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' HINT logbook_daily_user; hive tier raises 54000 'cumulative quota exceeded' + archive hint; 0 probe rows survived rollback

evidence.asserts: a slow read is shown as slow IN THIS VIEW - it never answers with a server-derived value it does not have yet
evidence.checked: WHY THIS ROW WAS RE-MEASURED. Its previous evidence was IDENTICAL to the V1 row's on the same page - a KPI-tile reading taken at page load - because the banking loop selected rows by oracle name and swept both views with one page-level measurement. Fourteen V2 rows across the platform carried a measurement of a view they never visited, which is R7's exact failure: a claim resting on something other than what it names. The count did not move; the evidence did. PASSES, measured on the thread itself. With the feed loaded and the delay then armed, clicking a post's reply control fired exactly one read - `community_replies?post_id=eq.0f78265c-602b-4c5a-b617-1e8d40e47a84&hive_id=eq.084c113b...&order=created_at.asc` - and `#thread-overlay` opened visible with **0 resolved**. While that read was pending the overlay showed loading vocabulary and asserted NO emptiness: no 'no replies yet', no zero reply count. So a reader opening a thread on a slow connection is told it is loading, not told the thread is empty. MEASURED WITH THE DELAY ARMED AFTER INITIAL LOAD, which is what makes a V2 view measurable at all. A modal or thread cannot be opened while the feed that renders its opener is still pending, so the fetch wrapper starts INERT and is armed only once the page has settled; the view is then opened and its OWN read is the one held in flight. Every reading below is refused unless `resolved === 0` at measurement time and at least one request was intercepted, so neither a vacuous run nor an already-resolved one can be reported as a pass. AND WHERE NUMERIC WRITES ARE COUNTED, THEY ARE ATTRIBUTED BY CONTAINMENT: each write's ancestor chain is walked and only writes landing INSIDE this view's container count, so a page-level write cannot credit or convict the wrong view. The observer writes its own '4242' sentinel and the reading is REFUSED unless it sees it - a control that refused this very batch once, when the config was passed to the MutationObserver constructor instead of observe(), so observe() threw and the observer silently never attached. An unattached observer reports zero writes on every page.

evidence.asserts: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible
evidence.checked: PASSES. WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): OBJECT-level access: the gate's cross-tenant READ and OWN-SCOPE WRITE checks - read_logbook_xhive and read_cxp_xhive (a FOREIGN hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows) and logbook_edit_ownscope (a member cannot UPDATE another hive's logbook entry). These are per-OBJECT refusals: the caller names a specific row they do not own and is refused, which is exactly what BOLA asks. Persona under test on this row: anon (read boundary) - and the gate's probe IS that persona, a real authenticated member of one hive reaching for another's data. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of those checks returning a row it should not, and the gate is known to fire because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught - 1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, and a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the instrument the platform already owns instead of writing another: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. Current result: 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS ROLE-CORRECT, which is the only reason it means anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims. A probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction - and that is not hypothetical, it cost a false finding on this very platform the same day, when an approved change order looked EDITABLE as `postgres` and is in fact refused for both a worker and a supervisor, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path. IT IS RESEED-ROBUST: the actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot quietly turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the WRONG reason and read as a pass. AND IT CARRIES NO-REGRESSION CHECKS (join_rpc_ok, founder_create_ok), so a gate that 'passed' by breaking the legitimate path would be caught rather than celebrated. WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE: it was hand-walked in an earlier session and banked with no `evidence.replay`, so nothing could re-earn it without a human repeating the whole probe. It now carries the command, which is the entire point of the A16 anti-stale discipline: 546 db-anchored rows on this platform are in exactly that position, and this is 176 of them coming out of it.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 2 of its 5 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - community_xp (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows); hive_audit_log (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 9 read relation(s), 5 were probed live at the gateway (community_posts, community_reactions, community_replies, community_xp, hive_audit_log).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. evidence.asserts: FIXED THIS WALK. Half the users were already served: a supervisor sees a toggle reading 'Share with all WorkHive teams' with the consequence spelled out beneath it, 'Public posts appear on the Global tab for every hive', plus a lock-reason line for when Announcements force it on. A worker saw NONE of that. The row carries display:none and is revealed only inside `if (HIVE_ROLE === 'supervisor')`, so an ordinary member composed a post with nothing on screen about where it would go, on a board named 'community' where the reasonable assumption is that everyone can read it. Their posts do in fact stay private - isPublic is `HIVE_ROLE === 'supervisor' && checkbox.checked`, so a worker's post can never be public - which makes the silence a missed reassurance rather than a leak, but the oracle is about what the member KNOWS before an act they cannot undo, not about what the system happens to do. The composer now tells them: 'This stays inside your hive. Only your hive-mates can read it, and it will not appear on the public Global feed.' It is hidden for supervisors in the same branch that reveals their toggle, because two elements describing one fact differently is the defect this platform keeps re-finding.
evidence.checked: Traced the actual default rather than inferring it from the hidden control, since a hidden checkbox reading false and a role gate that ignores the checkbox entirely are different guarantees: the write path computes isPublic from the ROLE first, so the worker case is closed in code, not merely unticked in the DOM. Confirmed the toggle's reveal is the sole supervisor branch, so no other path shows it. The new note and the supervisor toggle are mutually exclusive by construction - the branch that displays one hides the other - which was checked as an edit rather than assumed, because leaving both visible would have a supervisor reading 'this stays inside your hive' directly above a control offering to publish it. Both inline script blocks re-parsed after the edit.

subject.name: anon limits are stated as limits

scenarios.oracle: an anon reader's limits are stated as limits, never rendered as emptiness

evidence.asserts: FIXED THIS WALK. The oracle asks that an anonymous reader's limits be stated AS limits rather than rendered as emptiness. Community never rendered emptiness, but it did something no better: it bounced the visitor with `window.location.href = 'index.html'` and no reason, so someone following a link to the board landed on the marketing homepage with nothing explaining why. That reads as 'this page does not exist', not 'you need to sign in'. The platform already had the answer and this line simply missed it - asset-hub, analytics, alert-hub, dayplanner, analytics-report and ai-quality all redirect to `index.html?signin=1`, and index.html:3586 reads that parameter and opens the sign-in modal, so the limit announces itself. The sharpest part is that community's OWN NEXT LINE, the _authUid gate two lines below, already passed the parameter: which of the two gates a visitor happened to trip decided whether they were told anything. Both now prompt. achievements.html carried the identical omission on both its .then and .catch branches and was fixed with it, since one page telling a signed-out visitor to sign in while its sibling drops them on a homepage is the same defect wearing a different file name.
evidence.checked: Verified the parameter is actually CONSUMED before relying on it, rather than assuming a convention from its use elsewhere - `?signin=1` could easily have been decoration that nothing reads, which is the declared-but-never-wired shape this codebase has produced repeatedly. index.html:3586 reads it through URLSearchParams and calls openSignIn, so the redirect genuinely produces a prompt. Established the convention by counting real usages across the page set rather than picking a form I preferred, and confirmed community's adjacent gate already used it, which is what makes this an omission rather than a design choice. Both edited pages re-parsed clean.
evidence.value_checked: before, community:897: index.html (no param) | community:899, two lines below: index.html?signin=1 | platform usages of ?signin=1: asset-hub, analytics, alert-hub, dayplanner, analytics-report, ai-quality | consumer: index.html:3586 URLSearchParams('signin')==='1' -> openSignIn | achievements:539-540 both branches lacked it | after: community 2 occurrences, achievements 3, all gates prompt

findings.title: TRACED: the .wh-avatar overflow is the avatar's OWN centred text, not the level badge - and it is a consequence of this session's overflow:visible fix
findings.detail: THREE PROBES, AND THE FIRST TWO WERE WRONG - recording the chain because the wrong answers were the plausible ones. (1) I assumed the badge: .wh-avatar-lvl is positioned bottom:-8px to hang below the circle and the avatar had overflow:hidden, so the two rules fought. That WAS a real defect - 21% of every level pill clipped across 32 avatars, digits cut - and fixing it (mask moved to .wh-avatar > img, container set to overflow:visible) was correct and is verified: 0 pills clipped on community and achievements. (2) I then assumed the badge also explained the horizontal scrollWidth excess and widened my probe's absolute-child exclusion to DESCENDANTS. That made the readings WORSE - community 14 -> 22, achievements 11 -> 20 - because the badge is centred with translateX(-50%) and never passes the avatar's right edge: measured layout box right edge 61 against clientWidth 64 (3px INSIDE), painted box right edge 48. I reverted it rather than add a third guess. (3) THE DECISIVE TEST, which should have been first: remove the suspect and see if the symptom goes. Hiding the pill, removing only its transform, and pulling it fully inside vertically ALL left scrollWidth 84 against clientWidth 64 - a 20px excess completely unchanged in every case. So the badge contributes nothing to it. THE ACTUAL CAUSE: .wh-avatar is `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center` with its initials as a direct text node. A centred flex item wider than its container overflows EQUALLY ON BOTH SIDES, so text ~104px wide in a 64px content box spills ~20px each way and scrollWidth reads 64 + 20 = 84 - which is exactly the measurement. The excess is the avatar's own label being wider than the circle. AND THIS IS A SIDE EFFECT OF MY OWN FIX, stated plainly rather than left for someone to find: under the previous overflow:hidden those oversized initials were CLIPPED to the circle; under overflow:visible they now SPILL outside it. Both the badge and the text were sharing one overflow property for opposite purposes, and no single value satisfies both. TO CLOSE, and it needs a look at the rendering rather than another measurement: identify which avatars actually carry oversized labels (the sample here shows initials like 'PA' fitting and glyph labels like the star tier badges running wide), then constrain the LABEL - a max-width with a smaller font-size or a single-glyph cap - so the text fits the circle while the badge keeps hanging below it. Constraining the text is the fix; putting the clip back would re-break the badge.
findings.observed: avatar clientWidth 64 / scrollWidth 84 / excess 20, unchanged with the pill hidden, un-transformed, or moved inside; pill layout right edge 61 vs clientWidth 64

findings.title: RESOLVED - NOT A DEFECT: the .wh-avatar overflow is a decorative spinning tier halo drawn by a PSEUDO-ELEMENT, structurally invisible to any DOM walk
findings.detail: FOUR PROBES, AND THE FIRST THREE WERE WRONG. Recording the whole chain because the wrong answers were each more plausible than the right one, and the shape of the error is the lesson. GUESS 1 - the level badge. .wh-avatar-lvl is positioned bottom:-8px to hang below the circle while the avatar had overflow:hidden, so the two rules fought. That WAS a real defect and the fix stands, verified: 21% of every level pill had been clipped across 32 avatars, and 0 are clipped now. But it did not explain the horizontal excess. GUESS 2 - the badge again, via my probe. I widened the absolute-child exclusion to DESCENDANTS to absorb it, and the readings got WORSE: community 14 -> 22, achievements 11 -> 20. Measured, the badge's layout box ends at 61 against clientWidth 64 - three pixels INSIDE - and its painted box at 48. Reverted. GUESS 3 - the avatar's own centred text. .wh-avatar is display:flex with justify-content:center, and a centred flex item wider than its box overflows equally BOTH ways, which would make scrollWidth = clientWidth + 2x the spill. Arithmetically perfect and factually wrong: the initials 'PA' measure 21px in a 64px box via a Range, and 0 of 20 avatars have text wider than their container. THE DECISIVE TEST, which should have been probe 1: remove the suspect and re-read. Hiding the pill, removing its transform, and pulling it inside all left the excess UNCHANGED at 20px - so the badge was exonerated by measurement long before I stopped blaming it. Then, forcing `content: none` on both pseudo-elements took scrollWidth from 91 to EXACTLY 64 = clientWidth. THE CAUSE: .wh-tier-legend::after is an 84x84 ring at inset:-10px with animation wh-spin, plus a 72x72 ::before, on a 72px avatar - a decorative rotating halo marking the top tier. It is intentional, it is aria-invisible, and it is a PSEUDO-ELEMENT, so no querySelectorAll('*') walk can ever see it. That is why three rounds of DOM reasoning failed: I was looking for the contributor among elements, and the contributor is not an element. VERDICT: THERE IS NO OVERFLOW DEFECT ON THESE PAGES. The rows stay owed only because the probe needs a fifth exclusion - skip a self-overflow whose excess disappears when ::before/::after content is suppressed - and that exclusion must be written and self-tested, not assumed. THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: scrollWidth is a rendering fact, not a DOM fact. Before attributing it to any element, test by SUBTRACTION - remove the candidate and see whether the number moves. A DOM walk cannot see pseudo-elements, generated content, or a transformed paint box, so reasoning from the element tree will confidently name the wrong culprit.
findings.observed: wh-tier-legend: clientWidth 64, scrollWidth 91 (excess 27) -> 64 with ::before/::after content suppressed. ::after 84x84 inset:-10px animation wh-spin; ::before 72x72 inset:-4px. Badge and text both exonerated by subtraction (excess unchanged at 20px without the pill; 0 of 20 avatars have text wider than their box)

findings.title: DENOMINATOR CORRECTED 25 -> 31 tab stops; verdict unchanged at 0 without an indicator
findings.detail: THE PREVIOUS SWEEP UNDER-COUNTED THIS DENOMINATOR, and the cause was a break where a continue belonged. Focus order on these pages runs shared chrome, then BODY, then the page own controls - so a loop that treated a BODY-focus stop as the end of the tab ring stopped walking before reaching any page control. On assistant that reported ZERO stops against 9 real ones and I held the row back as either vacuous or a WCAG 2.1.1 failure; it was neither, it was my loop. Re-run with BODY as a CONTINUE, a 120-press budget and a 25-press no-new-stop stall guard. On this page the truncation cost 6 stops (25 counted, 31 real). The VERDICT is unchanged - 0 of 31 lacked a visible indicator on the full walk - so the row is not withdrawn. But the banked denominator was narrower than the page, and a narrowed denominator is the exact flaw this bank exists to catch: 0 failing over a subset is a weaker claim than 0 failing over the whole. Recorded rather than silently re-stamped, because the difference between those two claims is the whole point.

findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (16 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - the V3 drive re-opened V2 (composer-overlay), so banking it would record one walk under two row ids
findings.detail: The drive selects the SECOND distinct onclick opener precisely so that V2 and V3 are different views. On this page only ONE such opener is visible in the default state, so the selection fell back to the first and re-opened composer-overlay - the exact artefact V2 was measured on. Banking that as V3 would record a single walk twice under two ids: coverage would rise while evidence did not, which is the same dishonesty as counting a walked cell as a banked cell. THIS IS NOT A PAGE DEFECT. The page has further views - the roadmap names community thread-overlay / report-overlay / person-overlay, and pm-scheduler pm-edit-modal / add-task-sheet - they are simply not reachable from the default state because their openers attach to rendered rows that need data. Same denominator-grows-with-population effect measured elsewhere today. TO RESOLVE: name this page V3 opener explicitly instead of discovering it generically, or seed the surface so a second row-level opener exists to click. Row stays owed.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.
