findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

observed.instrument: tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5 (66 pairs walked, 16 reached a composer)
observed.why: no composer reachable for this identity on this page
observed.not_green_because: a journey that cannot be constructed is unbuilt, not passing
observed.to_settle: add the missing composer to dialog_targets.mjs, or declared-na under R10 with the CO family as replacement

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs - the capture surface is opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, and then ABANDONED BY RELOAD. Pressing a modal's X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what actually happens when someone takes a call or their phone dies, and it is the one path no confirm dialog can intercept. ★THREE SHAPES ARE CHECKED SEPARATELY because each needs a different fix: a ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST (psql, against this run's marker); a DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT (fields return pre-filled with no label, so the person cannot tell whether their work was SAVED or merely REMEMBERED); and a QUEUED WRITE that drains later. A restored draft is the GOOD design - it is judged on whether the surface LABELS it, never on whether it restores. ★AND THE PROBE PROVES ITS OWN FILL LANDED, so a green cannot be vacuous: an unfilled form makes 'no half-applied state' trivially true. My first logbook case invented an opener and a field that do not exist and came back UNGRADED rather than passing on an empty fill; the real controls were then read from tools/dialog_targets.mjs and the pages' own ids.  ★THIS IS THE HIGHEST-STAKES ABANDON ON THE ROSTER, which is why it is worth stating plainly: every other half-applied write in this family is visible only on its author's own screen. A half-written POST that lands anyway is PUBLISHED TO OTHER PEOPLE, and cannot be quietly corrected afterwards. FOR THIS PAGE: a post, abandoned mid-compose. Filled, abandoned by reload, and on return: 0 row(s) created, 0 field(s) pre-filled - no row was written and nothing came back pre-filled - a clean slate

evidence.asserts: a link that leaves this surface carries its context with it, and the receiving surface arrives in the state that context names rather than its default
evidence.checked: A live two-surface walk with a control. ORIGIN: this page links to 'marketplace.html?section=services' (community.html:618). DESTINATION: verified as a signed-in member (1 auth key in localStorage): Services active on arrival. THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS NON-VACUOUS: loaded WITHOUT the parameter the destination shows Parts active and Services inactive - Parts is the default - while WITH '?section=services' Parts goes inactive and Services becomes active. So the two arrivals are distinguishable states and the difference is exactly the context handed over. I NEARLY FILED THE OPPOSITE: a first comparison of character counts and a coarse tab-text list showed the two URLs as identical, and a grep for searchParams.get('section') returned nothing, which together read as 'five pages hand off a section the destination silently drops'. Reading TAB STATE rather than tab text disproved it - the absence of a grep match is not evidence about behaviour. Read-only: page loads only, nothing written; each identity used a fully separate browser context so none could inherit another's session or cache.
evidence.value_checked: origin link measured on the rendered page; destination tab STATE read (active/aria-selected) rather than tab text; with-param vs without-param compared as the control

evidence.asserts: a link that leaves this surface carries its context with it, and the receiving surface arrives in the state that context names rather than its default
evidence.checked: A live two-surface walk with a control. ORIGIN: this page links to 'marketplace.html?section=services' (community.html:618). DESTINATION: verified for TWO distinct signed-in identities in separate browser contexts - supervisor and worker, each with its own session - and BOTH arrived with Services active, so the handoff is per-identity rather than working only for whoever produced the link. THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS NON-VACUOUS: loaded WITHOUT the parameter the destination shows Parts active and Services inactive - Parts is the default - while WITH '?section=services' Parts goes inactive and Services becomes active. So the two arrivals are distinguishable states and the difference is exactly the context handed over. I NEARLY FILED THE OPPOSITE: a first comparison of character counts and a coarse tab-text list showed the two URLs as identical, and a grep for searchParams.get('section') returned nothing, which together read as 'five pages hand off a section the destination silently drops'. Reading TAB STATE rather than tab text disproved it - the absence of a grep match is not evidence about behaviour. Read-only: page loads only, nothing written; each identity used a fully separate browser context so none could inherit another's session or cache.
evidence.value_checked: origin link measured on the rendered page; destination tab STATE read (active/aria-selected) rather than tab text; with-param vs without-param compared as the control

findings.title: submit control sits behind a form the probe did not fill
findings.detail: MEASURED, NOT BANKED - kept so the next session does not re-derive it. tools/prove_double_fire.mjs reached this page with all writes intercepted and held (nothing could be written), but no visible enabled control with a write verb on this page The submit control on this page lives BEHIND a form or modal that must be opened AND filled before it will attempt a write, so a top-level press only opens a view. UNGRADED rather than failed: reporting "no double-fire guard" about a control that never submits anything is a fabricated defect. TO CLOSE THIS ROW the harness needs a per-page flow that opens the form, fills the minimum valid fields, and THEN double-presses - with the same write interception, which is what makes doing so safe.
